macroForm.fairUseNotice: Use macros only while you are present and supervising. Unattended botting, anti-cheat evasion, exploits, and activity prohibited by the target service are not allowed.
macroForm.help.activationRoles: When a macro starts, it runs for every assigned role that is launched and controllable. At least one role must be available; unavailable roles are skipped.
macroForm.help.activationModes: Tap to toggle switches between starting and stopping. With Tap or hold, a tap completes at least one run, while holding keeps a looping macro active until release.
macroForm.help.activationRepeat: A loop waits and starts its next run only after the full step sequence finishes. A 0 ms interval removes only the extra wait; input timing and browser scheduling still apply.
macroForm.help.callsRequirements: A called macro uses its own assigned roles. Every called macro must be enabled and assigned, and macro calls cannot form a cycle.
macroForm.help.callsWait: Wait for completion runs the child macro once and resumes the parent after it finishes. Keys held until stopped are released at the end of that run.
macroForm.help.callsTrigger: Trigger and continue uses the child macro's repeat setting without making the parent wait. Interrupting the parent stops its triggered descendants; when the parent completes normally, they continue running.
macroForm.help.callsDuplicate: Triggering a child macro that is already running does not start or create another run.
macroForm.help.stopRun: Stopping a macro ends the same run across all assigned roles and releases keys held by that macro.
macroForm.help.stopChild: Stopping a child in Wait for completion cancels the parent. Stopping a Trigger and continue child does not stop the parent.
macroForm.help.stopRole: Closing any participating role stops the entire multi-role macro run and its descendants that are still owned by it.

settings.title: Settings
settings.aboutLegalDescription: Review app identity, legal documents, privacy practices, and third-party software notices.
settings.description: Adjust interface, game, data, and update settings without changing existing role data.
settings.interfaceDescription: Choose the app theme, interface language, browser fonts, and workspace appearance.
settings.gameDescription: Set defaults used when creating roles and launching game browsers.
settings.macrosDescription: Set reliable input timing for macros with shortcuts and the default wait used when enabling loops.
settings.macroStartupDelayDescription: For a macro with a shortcut, wait once after input focus is ready and before its first step. A called macro applies this only when it has its own shortcut.
settings.macroKeyHoldDescription: For macros with shortcuts, keep each key down before sending key up so frame-based games can observe the input.
settings.macroPostInputDelayDescription: For macros with shortcuts, reserve the role's input queue after every key release or completed click before another macro input can run.
settings.macroDefaultLoopDelayDescriptio: Prefill this value when a macro is changed from run once to loop. Existing macros are not rewritten.

settings.macroRecommendedMinimum: For reliable browser-game input, we recommend at least {value} ms.
settings.macroTimingNotice: The first three timing settings apply only to macros with shortcuts. 0 ms means no configured extra wait, not zero elapsed time. Browser scheduling can make every delay longer. Running macros keep the settings captured when they started.

browserEngine.capabilityMatrixEmpty: Launch a role to inspect the resolved engine and its current capability snapshot.
settings.graphicsRiskWarning: These settings favor high frame rates and can increase power use, tearing, driver instability, black screens, or the attack surface of trusted game sites.
settings.graphicsPreferHighPerformanceGp: Requests the discrete or high-performance GPU when one is available. Flag: --force-high-performance-gpu.
settings.graphicsForceGpuRasterizationDe: Requests GPU-backed page and Canvas rasterization. Flag: --enable-gpu-rasterization.
settings.graphicsFrameRateLimitDescripti: When disabled, Chromium receives --disable-frame-rate-limit and may render above the display refresh rate.
Always enabled on macOS because Chromium's unlimited-frame-rate flag can crash the GPU process.
settings.graphicsVsyncDescription: When disabled, Chromium receives --disable-gpu-vsync; tearing and GPU use can increase.
settings.graphicsVsyncRequiresFrameLimit: VSync remains disabled while the frame-rate limiter is disabled.
settings.graphicsWindowsEcoQosDescriptio: Keeps WebView2's power-efficient scheduling for background processes. Turning this off applies --disable-features=UseEcoQoSForBackgroundProcess to newly created WebView2 environments. Power use and heat may increase.
settings.graphicsGpuBlocklistDescription: When disabled, Chromium receives --ignore-gpu-blocklist and may use drivers it considers unstable.
settings.graphicsUnsafeWebGpuDescription: Enables WebGPU without Chromium's normal safety guarantees. Flag: --enable-unsafe-webgpu.
settings.graphicsDriverWorkaroundsDescri: Keep enabled for stability. Disabling adds --disable-gpu-driver-bug-workarounds.
settings.graphicsBackendDescription.wind: Choose Chromium's Windows ANGLE backend. Vulkan also enables the native Vulkan implementation.
